html:
The bank of the Medici family of Florence, founded by Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici in 1397 and the most powerful bank in Europe for much of the 1400s. It collapsed in 1494.

It had branches in Rome, Venice, Geneva, Bruges, London, Avignon and elsewhere. Its biggest client was the papacy, whose revenues it collected and moved across Europe. It also traded in cloth, alum and silk, and used bills of exchange and double-entry bookkeeping, methods that went back to the Champagne fairs.

The bank's profits made the Medici the rulers of Florence in all but name. Cosimo de' Medici spent heavily on buildings and scholars and helped bring the Council of Florence to the city. His grandson Lorenzo the Magnificent was patron to Botticelli and the young Michelangelo.

Under Lorenzo the bank declined, through bad loans to kings such as Edward IV of England, weak branch managers and his own neglect. When the French invaded Italy in 1494, the Medici were driven out of Florence and the bank failed. The family later returned to rule.
sum: The bank of the Medici family of Florence, founded by Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici in 1397 and the most powerful bank in Europe for much of the 1400s. It collapsed in 1494.
